# Stage: actors and verbs

A storyboard is a show written down: an ordered list of entries, each naming a scene, how long it stays and how it leaves. The Director walks whatever list it is handed, and where it is handed none it writes one as it goes from the seed, so the seeded show is a storyboard nobody wrote down. A note's is kept in its own folder as JSON and written in its timeline beside Play (`NoteStoryboard`); `--storyboard <path>` plays a file, YAML or JSON.

## How one is written

- **Sampled ranges.** Anywhere a number is expected, `[lo, hi]` is a range, sampled once per instance from the seed: the same song plays the same show, and another seed rolls a fresh variation of everything left as a range. A two-number list is always a range; positions are `[x, y, z]`.
- **defs / use.** `defs:` is a top-level map of named fragments; `use: <name>` inside any map deep-merges the fragment under the map's own keys (its own keys win), and a map that is only `{use: name}` becomes the fragment. Fragments may use fragments (a cycle is refused).
- **How long an entry stays.** A fixed `hold` in seconds, or `exit` on a musical cue (`beat`, `movement`, `lull`, bounded by `min_hold` / `max_hold`), or neither: the scene's own lifecycle. `sensitivity` is the tempo: every hold and every stage track compresses with it, so each event still lands.
- **A loop or the song.** `loop: true` starts again from the first entry. Off, the show follows the song: it cycles the `tail` after the sequence and rolls back to the top when the song does.
- **The stage.** `scene: stage` is the one made of data: its `cast` (actors from the Cast registry, each with a unique `id` and a `kind`; one that appears mid-entry is declared `hidden: true`) and its `track` (spans of verbs from the Actions registry, timed in the track's `nominal` seconds and scaled to the entry's length). Consecutive stage entries carry their live actors across the cut where ids match - the same body, pose and latched verbs - unless an entry says `carry: false`.

## Fields

What a storyboard can say, read from the tables its editor builds its rows from (`Storyboard.BOARD` and its siblings in [src/stage/storyboard.gd](../src/stage/storyboard.gd)): a field in a table is a control in the editor. A `num` is a number or a sampled `[lo, hi]` range; a key left out is its default.

### The storyboard

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loop` | Loop | bool | At the end, start again from the first entry. Off, the show follows the song instead: it holds its last entry, or cycles the tail, and rolls back to the top when the song does. |
| `transition` | Transition | enum: `cut`, `dip`, `fade` | How one entry gives way to the next unless the entry says otherwise: a hard cut, a dip through black, or a crossfade. Two entries that can morph always do. |
| `sensitivity` | Tempo | float | The story's pace. Higher is faster: every hold shrinks and every entry's timeline is compressed with it, so each event still lands. What an actor does on its own never speeds up. |
| `elastic` | Elastic | float | How far a stage's timeline breathes with the song: a loud passage runs it faster, a quiet one slower, the total unchanged. 0 keeps it even. |

### An entry

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scene` | Scene | scene | What is on screen. Stage is the one made of data: its actors and what they do are written in the entry itself. |
| `behavior` | Motion | enum: `static`, `drift`, `fluid` | How the scene moves: held still, drifting as one, or every part moving on its own. |
| `shot` | Shot | enum: `centered`, `offset`, `push_in`, `pull_back`, `pan`, `canted` | How the camera frames it. Left unset, one that suits the scene is drawn from the entry's seed. |
| `seed` | Seed | int | Pins everything the scene rolls - its colors, its shapes, each sampled range. Unset, it comes from the song and the entry's place in the list. |
| `transition` | Leaves by | enum: `cut`, `dip`, `fade` | How this entry gives way to the next. Unset, the storyboard's own transition. |
| `sensitivity` | Tempo | float | This entry's own pace. Unset, the storyboard's. |

### How long an entry stays

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hold` | Seconds | float | How long the entry stays. |
| `exit` | Cue | enum: `beat`, `movement`, `lull` | What the entry leaves on: a beat, a change of section, or a drop into quiet. |
| `min_hold` | At least | float | The entry never leaves sooner than this many seconds. |
| `max_hold` | At most | float | The entry leaves by this many seconds even if no cue came. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `carry` | Carry | bool | Actors with the same id as the entry before carry on across the cut - the same body, pose and gaze. Off, the entry opens on a clean cut. |
| `elastic` | Elastic | float | This entry's own breathing with the song. Unset, the storyboard's. |

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eye` | Eye | vec3 | Where the camera stands. |
| `look` | Looks at | vec3 | The point it faces. |

### An actor

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Name | text | What the timeline calls this actor. One name, one body: the same name in the next stage entry is the same actor, carried across. |
| `kind` | Kind | enum: `eye`, `prism`, `swarm` | What it is. |
| `at` | Place | vec3 | Where it stands: right, up and toward the camera. With the camera at its default, 0.62 to either side are the two side-by-side places. |
| `hidden` | Starts hidden | bool | It is there but unseen until something on the timeline reveals it. |
| `seed` | Seed | int | Pins what this actor rolls for itself. Unset, it comes from the entry's seed. |

### A span

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | Does | enum: `look`, `blink`, `arrive`, `sprout`, `split`, `crystallize`, `tremble`, `burst`, `lock`, `desync`, `hold_still`, `sway`, `counterflow`, `specialize`, `form`, `leave`, `gather`, `fly`, `helix_split`, `lane_jump`, `set`, `ramp`, `pulse`, `flash` | What happens. |
| `target` | Who | targets | The actors it happens to. None chosen means everyone on the stage. |
| `ease` | Ease | enum: `smooth`, `linear`, `in`, `out`, `spike` | The shape of its progress across the window. A verb with phases of its own wants linear. |
| `on` | Waits for | enum: `beat`, `movement`, `lull` | A cue in the music the span waits for once its time has come, so a drop lands on the drop. |
| `by` | No later than | float | Seconds it waits for that cue before going anyway. |
| `sustain` | Keeps on | bool | After its window closes it carries on at full strength for the rest of the entry, instead of finishing. |

## Cast (actor registry)

Cast - the actor registry for data-driven scenes (see scenes/stage.gd).

The registry sibling of `Primitives` (forces), `Layer` (visuals) and `Shots` (framing), for performers: an actor wraps a live body (`EyeBody`, `PrismBody`, ...) with the state a storyboard's verbs steer (slot position, scale, hue, visibility, tempo), so choreography lives in the data (the track's action spans). Every numeric config value accepts a `[lo, hi]` range, sampled once per instance ("cattle, not pets").

An actor is a RefCounted, so a stage hands its live actors to the next stage through the morph payload and a body continues across a cut.

Verbs communicate with actors through `state` (a plain Dictionary): `state.tremble` (0..1 riser vibration), `state.lock_to` (pose-lock source id), `state.still` (spin damping), `state.pulse` ({amp, rate} scale breathing), `state.focus` (a world point the eye looks at), `state.mit` (a split under way, drawn as the eye's membrane or the prism's bond), `state.form` (its place in a formation, held by the stage - `Actions.Form.hold`), `state.upright` (a slow righting under way, held by the stage - `Actions.right`). Kind classes read what they understand; unknown keys are inert, so a misspelled verb cannot crash a show.

Registry: `Cast.REGISTRY` in [src/stage/cast.gd](../src/stage/cast.gd) (3 kinds)

### `eye` - EyeActor

A human eye (`EyeBody`) on a slot. Gaze is driven by a look verb feeding `state.focus` (shared focus = real vergence); when no verb has fed it for a moment it falls back to the body's own center-biased self-saccades.

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Size | num | How large the eye is. Unset, drawn between 0.24 and 0.34. |
| `hue` | Hue | num | The iris's color, around the wheel from 0 to 1. Unset, drawn from the seed. |

### `swarm` - SwarmActor

A formation of prisms streaming along an invisible track into the void: a group actor (many bodies, one performer), as the swarm's coordinated strand math is one thing, not N choreographies. Ported from prism_swarm.gd. Verbs steer it through state: `gather` (members ease in one at a time), `travel` (flown distance, the fly verb), `split_k` (the track opens into a double helix; the red strand fades in on the other winding), `lane` (the bank-and-jump to the far strand). config: count / count_red / spacing / head / size / helix / r_min / r_max / hue (blue strand) / hue_red / bank ("left" / "right"; by seed otherwise) / lead (an actor id whose live prism becomes member 0 across a carry).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `count_red` | Red members | num | How many fly in the red strand once the helix opens. Unset, as many as the blue. |
| `spacing` | Spacing | num | The distance between one member and the next along the track. |
| `head` | Head | num | How far ahead of the camera the formation's lead flies. |
| `size` | Size | num | How large each member is. |
| `helix` | Helix | num | How tightly the two strands wind once the track opens into a double helix. |

## Actions (verb registry)

Actions - the verb registry for data-driven scenes (see scenes/stage.gd).

The registry sibling of `Primitives` / `Layer` / `Shots`, for choreography: each verb is a small class applied to named actors over a time window by a `Track` span, called with data.

Lifecycle: `begin(stage, actors)` once when the window is entered, `apply(stage, actors, k, f, dt)` every frame with the eased window fraction k (a point span gets a single k=1 apply), `finish(stage, actors)` once when it closes. Most verbs latch on finish (a specialized prism stays specialized); undoing is another span.

Verbs receive their args raw (ranges intact) plus a seeded rng: values meant to be fixed per instance are sampled in begin() ("cattle, not pets"); per-event values (a gaze fixation's distance) are re-drawn as they happen. Same seed, same show.

Registry: `Actions.REGISTRY` in [src/stage/actions.gd](../src/stage/actions.gd) (24 verbs)

### `look` - Look

look - aim eyes at a wandering 3D focus point. All targets share one focus, so two eyes verge (toe in near, run parallel far); a rare stray sends one eye wandering. The depth-tier table comes from the args (see `Cast.FocusSampler`).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tiers` | Depths | data | Where the gaze rests, as a list of tiers: each a chance `p`, a distance `dist` and how long it dwells there, `dwell`. |
| `lateral` | Sideways | num | How far a fixation strays to the side. |
| `stray` | Stray | num | The chance that one eye wanders off the shared focus for a fixation. |

### `arrive` - Arrive

arrive - the actor flies in from off the frame, fast, and lands on its place like a rubber band coming home: past it, back, settling in a few quick swings. A prism flies apex first along its way and still points that way as it lands; at the end it latches a slow righting (`Actions.right`) that turns it upright over the next seconds while whatever follows goes on - in its last moments too, since a window that ends on its entry's cut never finishes. Give the span `ease: linear`: the verb shapes its own motion. args: from ([x,y,z] origin, default a sampled point off the frame), wobble (how far past its place it swings; default as far as its speed carries it), upright (the righting's seconds; 0 keeps it pointing the way it came).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | From | vec3 | Where it flies in from. Unset, from off the frame. |
| `wobble` | Swing | num | How far past its place it swings as it lands. Unset, as far as the speed it came in with carries it. |
| `upright` | Rights in | num | Seconds it takes, once landed, to turn gently from the way it flew in to upright, while whatever comes next goes on. 0 keeps it pointing the way it came. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:299](../src/stage/actions.gd#L299)

### `sprout` - Sprout

sprout - a standing rose beside the anchor: the stem grows up from below the frame (rooted in the void's floor, never from the camera), rises almost vertical beside the eye's anchor, crests above it and droops its head so the tip hangs downward; the eye swells at the tip like fruit, facing the ground. The bloom sheds a petal or two; then the eye detaches, which whips the freed stem back as it retreats down along itself while the dropped eye settles onto its anchor and rights itself to face forward. The vine and petals are drawn by `Cast.EyeActor` from `state.vine`. Give the span `ease: linear`. args: side (-1/1 stem side, default sampled).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | Side | num | Which side of its place the stem grows on: -1 left, 1 right. Unset, by the seed. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:373](../src/stage/actions.gd#L373)

### `split` - Split

split - mitosis: one eye divides into two. The twin buds off the source as a blank wet ball (no iris yet), connected by a stretching tissue membrane (drawn by `Cast.EyeActor` from `state.mit`); volume is conserved, so the parent deflates as the bud swells (one R eye -> two ~0.79R twins). The pull is stick-slip up to the SNAP, where the membrane tears: both eyes recoil on a damped spring to their slots, droplets spatter, and then the newborn's iris surfaces, followed by its first blink.

A prism divides by CLONING: the twin is the same size, shape and pose, in its own hue from the first frame, sharing the parent's every move until the bond between them tears; then it turns away on its own. Timed in seconds, so any window reads alike: a moment in place as the twin condenses over its parent, a quick pull to the bond's limit, a tug-of-war there that takes up the rest of the window (back and forth, the strands taut and quivering), the tear (shards, a flash), and a spring settle into each place. args: into (actor id), slots ([[x,y,z],[x,y,z]]), hue (the newborn's; default the parent's).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `into` | Into | actor | The hidden actor that becomes the newborn. |
| `hue` | Its hue | num | The color the newborn warms to as it pulls away. Unset, its parent's. |
| `slots` | Places | data | Where the two come to rest, as two places: `[[x, y, z], [x, y, z]]`. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:499](../src/stage/actions.gd#L499)

### `crystallize` - Crystallize

crystallize - the eye freezes over into the prism (a staged physical transition, not a crossfade). Phase 1, stilling: the gaze locks to one point and crystal edges creep across the ball (`Cast.EyeActor` draws the cage from `state.crys`) while the pupil constricts and the iris hue chills toward the crystal's. Phase 2, faceting: the cage tightens and glints, the iris features die away, and the prism's wireframe materializes aligned over it. Phase 3, collapse: the ball is sucked into the crystal's core (cold shards, an icy flash) and the prism solidifies alive. Give the span `ease: linear`. args: into (actor id).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `into` | Into | actor | The hidden prism the eye freezes over into. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:766](../src/stage/actions.gd#L766)

### `counterflow` - Counterflow

counterflow - the pair take opposite highways: each merges onto its own lane and cruises against the other (they pass mid-scene), rolling about its travel axis like a drill; in the final stretch each pulls a loop off its lane, the arc that carries them into the ouroboros. Cruise speed rides the actor's live time_scale, so a specialized small/fast prism zips while the large/slow one glides. Give the span `ease: linear`. args: lane (half-gap between the highways), speed (world/s), loop_k (where the exit loop begins, 0..1).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lane` | Lane | num | How far apart the two highways run. |
| `speed` | Speed | num | How fast they cruise. |
| `loop_k` | Loop at | num | How far through the window each pulls its closing loop, from 0 to 1. |

### `form` - Form

form - the targets fly to the places of a shape and turn to one heading as they go, like a squadron: each member points the way the whole shape points. A tetrahedron's places are the centers of the upward small tetrahedra of one subdivided as finely as its members need (`lattice`: four, its corners; ten, its corners and edge midpoints; twenty, its edge thirds and face centers), so members sized to their spacing (`fit`) meet corner to corner and read as one large tetrahedron, with no member where the shape has no node. A ring's places are round its rim, a line's abreast. Once formed the shape turns about its upright as one rigid body. It latches: the formation lives in each member's `state.form` and the stage holds it there every frame (`hold`), across a cut too, until a `leave` takes a member out. A `form` over members already in one carries it on from where it stands, so the same shape and size continue without a jump while the turning eases to the new rate. args: shape, size, fit, center, tilt (degrees), turn (turns a minute), stagger.

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | Shape | enum | What they make: a tetrahedron (its corners, then its edge midpoints, finer as more join, never a member where it has no node), a ring, or a line abreast. The first actor named takes the first place. |
| `size` | Size | num | How far apart its outermost places are, corner to corner. |
| `fit` | Fit | bool | Size the members to their spacing, so their corners meet and together they read as one large shape. |
| `center` | Center | vec3 | Where the shape stands. Unset, where its members are now, on average. |
| `tilt` | Lean | num | How far it leans back from the camera, in degrees, so its depth shows. |
| `turn` | Turns | num | How fast the whole turns about its upright once formed, in turns a minute. |
| `stagger` | Stagger | num | How much later each member sets off than the one before, as a share of the window. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:1020](../src/stage/actions.gd#L1020)

### `leave` - Leave

leave - the reverse of arrive: a brief wind-up (it draws back a little, turning its apex the way it will go), then a launch that gathers speed until it is gone, out of any formation it was in; a prism flies apex first, rolling about its way, its apex along the exact way it goes, in depth too (a way straight into the distance is seen end-on). The way may run in depth. Toward the camera it grows as it comes, on a path that leaves the frame while still farther than `NEAREST` from the lens (one that would come nearer first is turned sideways until it does not), and ends at the frame's edge. Away from the camera it shrinks into the distance and fades out over the end of its window, gone by then whether or not it reached an edge. Hidden once its whole body is past the frame's edge. Give the span `ease: linear`: the verb shapes its own motion. args: to (the way it goes, right, up and toward the camera; unset, away from the others on the stage), force (0 winds up slowly and eases away, 1 snaps back and throws, rolling fast and shedding shards as it goes).

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | Toward | vec3 | Which way it goes, right, up and toward the camera. Toward the camera it grows and leaves the frame's edge, never coming near the lens; away it shrinks and fades out. Unset, away from the others on the stage, by the seed. |
| `force` | Force | num | How hard it goes, from 0 to 1: low winds up slowly and eases away, high snaps back and throws, rolling fast and shedding shards. |

Source: [src/stage/actions.gd:1204](../src/stage/actions.gd#L1204)

pulse - a scale breathing on the target while the span runs ({amp, rate}); latches unless args.latch is false.

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amp` | Depth | num | How much its size breathes. |
| `rate` | Rate | num | How many breaths a second. |
| `latch` | Keeps on | bool | The breathing carries on after the window closes. |

## Track (the timeline runner)

Track - the timeline runner for data-driven scenes (see scenes/stage.gd).

A track is a list of spans, each applying one `Actions` verb to named actors over a time window. Times are authored in seconds of the track's nominal design length; at runtime they scale by `phase_span(nominal) / nominal`, so a storyboard's `hold` and `sensitivity` compress the whole timeline proportionally and every event still lands. Only the keyframe clock scales; the actors' ambient life runs on the raw delta.

Span fields (storyboard data): at            - a point event, or `from` / `to` for a window (nominal seconds) action        - an `Actions` registry key target        - actor id, list of ids, or "all" (the default) args          - the verb's config (ranges welcome) ease          - linear / smooth / in / out / spike (window fraction shaping) on            - optional musical cue gate: beat / movement / lull. The span arms at its start time and fires on the cue's next rising edge, so an event lands on the music by            - cue backstop, seconds after arming (default 1.5): if the cue never comes, fire anyway sustain       - true = after the window closes, keep applying at k = 1 for the rest of the scene instead of finishing (motion that must never park, e.g. a finale that keeps flying)

All range sampling draws from per-span rngs seeded off the scene rng in declaration order: same seed, same show, cue jitter aside.
